title: POLICE Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate reported version is repeated here.)

Protecting Our Lives by Initiating COPS Expansion Act of 2016 or the POLICE Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to expand the allowable use of grant funds under the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program to include participation in active shooter training programs.

summary.headline: A 2016 law lets federal Community Oriented Policing Services grant money be used for active shooter training programs.
summary.what_it_does: The POLICE Act changes the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968. It widens the list of permitted uses for grants under the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program. Under the change, local agencies that receive these grants may use the money to take part in active shooter training. The summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.group: State and local law enforcement agencies that receive COPS grants
who_it_affects.how: They may use COPS grant funds to pay for participation in active shooter training programs.

who_it_affects.group: Officers and other first responders in those agencies
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to take part in active shooter training that agencies pay for with COPS grant money.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on July 22, 2016. The summary does not list a separate effective date.
